cohort: The cohort consisted of 190 pregnant women diagnosed with term premature rupture of membranes (PROM) who were randomized into two management groups.
finding: Active management reduced the PROM-to-delivery interval and showed a trend toward reducing prolonged PROM-related complications and infection risk, while expectant management did not significantly increase adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Expectant management resulted in a higher proportion of full-term vaginal deliveries (81.1%) compared to active management (70.5%), though this difference was not statistically significant.
